Raises an alert if 9f2c...a1e4 runs on any host. Does not block it.
Nothing today. The file is on 1 host.
I changed it to an alert-only rule. If the file runs anywhere, you get an alert, and nothing is blocked. That is safe if the build owner turns out to own the file, but it will not stop a real repeat.

I limited the block to Windows hosts running Defend. The file is a Windows DLL, so Linux hosts are not at risk from it.

I lowered the change to medium. It still draws attention sooner than low, with less added noise.

I changed it to a logon restriction. Builds on the 2 build hosts keep working, and other hosts reject svc-build. That stops spread, but not use on the build hosts themselves.
